title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Theater on 1969-07-04
source: sbd > mc > d >cd > shn > wav > shn

ai_review.summary: Decent stereo audience recording with early fire on Hard To Handle and The Other One, but later drop‑outs and hiss hurt the listening experience.
ai_review.review: The July 4 1969 show captures a raw, high‑energy Dead at a crossroads of country‑cowboy tunes and psychedelic jams, highlighted by ripping performances of Hard To Handle, Cryptical → High Time, The Other One, Doin’ That Rag and the St. Stephen/Love Light pair.  Recording quality is solid at first – clear stereo mix with good balance – but deteriorates after the mid‑set as tape drop‑outs and left‑channel hiss make later songs difficult to enjoy.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is average with several standout moments; recording starts strong but suffers noticeable issues, leading to a combined rating in the mid‑range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part of tape is clear and well‑balanced stereo; after Doin' That Rag the mix drops out, left channel develops hiss and occasional drop‑outs, making later songs hard to hear.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set swings from high‑octane rockers into country‑flavored numbers and back into psychedelic jams; the early momentum is strong, but the second half loses steam both musically and due to recording degradation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers ripping guitar work and even plays pedal steel on several cuts; a brief vocal stumble (“swallowed a frog”) occurs during High Time.
band_member_comments.Bob: Front‑and‑center for most of the show, handling lead vocals on many numbers including Dire Wolf and several cowboy tunes.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten adds a distinctive touch on Casey Jones, noted as a memorable keyboard moment.
